extracted.intended_audience: journalists, future journalists, and teachers of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive page outlining the Poynter Institute's mission, program design, faculty, and learning outcomes for professional and aspiring journalists and journalism educators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small seminars / individual attention
rubrics_metrics.description: We keep seminars small, which means you get lots of individual attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit program design choice: small class size is presented as a core feature of the 'Poynter Experience' to ensure individualized instruction and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on instructional approach
rubrics_metrics.description: We emphasize a hands-on approach, so you participate in discussions, case studies, role-playing, and other exercises to get you involved in learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical, interactive methods (discussions, case studies, role-playing, exercises) are highlighted as essential to learning and skill development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty composition: resident and visiting professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Our resident faculty includes distinguished professionals and scholars, all master teachers who bring special expertise to every session. Each seminar also includes visiting faculty, accomplished professionals who leave their jobs for a week to help teach, who spend time with you inside and outside the classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of instruction is tied to a mix of experienced resident faculty and visiting practitioners who provide real-world perspectives and close mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial independence and mission-focus
rubrics_metrics.description: As a financially independent, nonprofit organization, the Institute is beholden to no interest except its own mission: to help journalists do their best work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional independence is presented as a safeguard for editorial and educational priorities; being nonprofit and independent is framed as a quality criterion for trustworthiness and mission fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: promote excellence and integrity in journalism and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poynter Institute is a school dedicated to teaching and inspiring journalists and media leaders. It promotes excellence and integrity in the practice of craft and in the practical leadership of successful businesses. It stands for a journalism that informs citizens and enlightens public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mission defines the Institute's evaluative standards: emphasis on excellence, integrity, informed citizenship, and leadership in media practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: courage to take risks
rubrics_metrics.description: The courage to take risks and to do your best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One stated outcome for participants; implies willingness to pursue ambitious reporting and editorial choices as a marker of program success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: higher self-esteem and career agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher sense of self-esteem and the power to shape your own career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to increase participants' confidence and ability to actively manage career trajectories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: new confidence in craft
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and practical gains in journalistic skill are a core expected result of participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: recognition of the value of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recognition of the value of diversity in the newsroom and in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness and appreciation of diversity are explicit program goals, framing inclusive practice as a quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: vocabulary to describe work and values
rubrics_metrics.description: The vocabulary to describe what you do and why, and what you stand for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing language to articulate professional roles and ethical stances is positioned as a measurable learning achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: desire to continue growth and share knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A desire to continue your growth as a journalist and to share what you've learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained professional development and mentorship/knowledge-sharing are expected long-term outcomes of the Institute's programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: network for ongoing support
rubrics_metrics.description: A new network of people who support you in your work, so your learning continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building professional networks is presented as an explicit benefit and metric of program success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: clear picture of journalism's role in democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear picture of the special role of journalism in a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic understanding and the normative role of journalism are named educational objectives, informing ethical and mission-driven practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: sense that one's work is valuable and impactful
rubrics_metrics.description: An understanding that your life's work is valuable and that you can make a difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivating professional purpose and perceived impact is an articulated outcome for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and levels of programs offered
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute has developed a rich mixture of teaching and research programs, ranging from sophisticated courses and seminars for professional journalists to basic classes at the elementary school level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breadth of offerings (from professional development to elementary-level education) and the sophistication of courses serve as program quality indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning environments and participant experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Seminar participants enjoy the variety of learning environments at the Institute: the intense discussion in the seminar rooms, the social interaction in the Great Hall, and the one-to-one conversation in the many small 'break-out' areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Varied physical and social learning settings (intense seminar discussion, social interaction, one-on-one conversations) are highlighted as part of the educational model and outcomes (e.g., leaving with a sense of mission rooted in a sense of place).

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding values: excellence, editorial integrity, independent ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Nelson Poynter insisted on excellence, editorial integrity, and independent ownership. Poynter willed the controlling stock of the Times Publishing Company to the Institute to assure its continued independence and to commit the publishing company's dividends to elevate the standards of journalism through training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and governance choices (founder's values, ownership structure) are presented as institutional standards that support the Institute's credibility and long-term commitment to journalistic quality.
